chunk_findings.detail: The regression test depends on real wall-clock timing with very little slack: it sets `LEASE_TICK_S` to `0.3` and `suite_wait_s` to `1.5`, then requires at least three `on_tick` calls. If the waiting process is delayed by roughly `0.6` seconds or more before the ticker starts or before the first tick (for example, lock-file I/O, thread scheduling, or a loaded CI runner), the waiter can time out after only two ticks, making `assert len(ticks) >= 3` fail even though the lease-tick feature is working. This makes the test nondeterministic/flaky rather than a reliable regression test.

chunk_findings.detail: The fix is only a hook: `on_tick` defaults to `None`, and the manifest contains no call-site change that passes it. A gate run that calls `suitelock.hold(...)` as before therefore executes `tick = _ticker(None)` and every `tick()` in the queue loop is a no-op, so a run queued for hours still lets its lease go idle—exactly B55ed1848d1. The new test passes an explicit callable and proves the helper works, but it does not demonstrate the bug is fixed for the gate-run path.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_no_tick_is_called_without_a_callable` does not actually test that no tick is called. It creates a local `ticks` list, but never passes it to `SL.hold` as `on_tick`, so `ticks` remains empty no matter what `SL.hold` does. For example, if `SL.hold` were changed to invoke a default/global tick path three times when no `on_tick` argument is supplied, this test would still pass because the assertion only compares the untouched local list to `[]`.

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds optional `on_tick`/`tick_s` support, but `tick_s` defaults to `0`, and the manifest contains no change to the gate-run caller that produced B55ed1848d1. With `tick_s=0`, `_ticker` returns a no-op (`tick_s <= 0` short-circuits), so the reported production path—`ddflow gate run unit_tests` waiting in the suite-lock queue—still calls `hold(...)` without enabling renewal and can still let its lease go idle after hours. The fix is therefore not wired end-to-end; the new unit test exercises the helper directly, not the queued gate-run path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: The first regression test only asserts `len(ticks) >= 3` and never uses the `time.monotonic()` values it stores, so it can pass if `SL.hold` calls `on_tick` three times in a burst before or at the start of the wait and then never ticks again while the run is queued. That would still reproduce the bug being fixed — no lease renewal during the hours-long queue — because the assertion only proves “some ticks happened,” not “ticks happened repeatedly during the wait.” A concrete wrong implementation satisfying this test is a ticker that fires three immediate ticks and then stops; the test would pass even though the lease would go idle while waiting.

chunk_findings.detail: The new span assertion `ticks[-1] - ticks[0] >= 2 * tick_s` does not actually prove that ticks were spread over the 2s queue wait; it only proves a span of 0.2s for `tick_s=0.1`. A wrong `SL.hold` ticker that calls `on_tick` three times at `t=0`, `0.1`, and `0.2` and then stops while the lock remains busy for the remaining ~1.8s passes both `len(ticks) >= 3` and the span assertion, so the regression test would not fail for the bug it claims to guard (no lease renewal during a long wait).

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that a raising `on_tick` must not end the suite-lock wait, but it only asserts that `SL.SuiteBusy` is raised and that `ticks == []`. Because the supplied `on_tick` is `lambda: 1 / 0`, it cannot record anything before raising, so `ticks == []` is true both when the tick is never called and when the tick is called but its exception aborts the wait loop. For example, if `_ticker` catches `ZeroDivisionError` and then breaks out of the wait loop, `hold` can raise `SuiteBusy` after the first ~0.1s tick instead of waiting the configured 0.6s; the test still sees `SuiteBusy` and an empty `ticks` list and passes, so this regression guard is vacuous for the behavior it names.
